macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks plunge as AI selloff intensifies
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.59%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.13%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.85% on Friday. The declines confirmed corrections in the S&P 500 and Dow as investor concerns over AI valuations deepened.

items.title: Fed officials signal support for higher interest rates
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook argued that the current policy rate is insufficient to address inflation, while other Fed officials also called for another increase. Markets are pricing in a high probability of a rate hike at the December meeting.

items.title: Asian markets fall sharply after Wall Street selloff
items.summary: Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell nearly 5%, South Korea’s Kospi declined 5.2%, and Hong Kong shares also dropped as global risk aversion spread. Semiconductor stocks were hit especially hard, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each falling more than 6%.

items.title: U.S. manufacturing momentum weakens while price pressures rise
items.summary: The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9, with new orders moving into contraction. Prices paid rose sharply, while initial jobless claims increased to 203,000 and continuing claims reached 1.763 million.

items.title: Anthropic IPO fails to calm AI-market concerns
items.summary: Anthropic shares initially jumped 17.1% from their $83 offering price, but the debut did not prevent a broader technology selloff. Nvidia and AMD fell sharply as investors questioned AI investment valuations and AMD’s China exposure.

items.title: Alibaba posts mixed results amid heavy AI investment
items.summary: Alibaba reportedly exceeded revenue expectations, helped by strong growth in its AI cloud business, but missed profit forecasts as investment costs remained elevated.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 as crypto sell-off intensifies
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped about 4.7% in 24 hours to roughly $59,467, briefly reaching $58,678, its first move below $60,000 in about four months. Ethereum fell approximately 6.5% to $1,643.6 amid broader risk-off trading and ETF outflows.

items.title: Major cryptocurrencies post steep losses
items.summary: Bitcoin fell 10.31% and Ethereum declined 9.49% over the reported period, while market liquidations increased as equities weakened. XRP also dropped sharply, while Solana showed relative strength with a reported 5.03% 24-hour gain despite remaining in a broader downtrend.

items.title: Backpack receives approval for blockchain-based derivatives exchange
items.summary: Crypto exchange Backpack received approval from the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission to establish what it describes as the first blockchain-based derivatives exchange in the United States, using unified global liquidity.

items.title: Hong Kong advances virtual-asset licensing requirements
items.summary: Hong Kong gazetted legislation requiring virtual-asset dealing, advisory, management and custody providers to obtain licenses or registration with the Securities and Futures Commission.

items.title: Binance-linked hackers move hundreds of millions in Ether
items.summary: Wallets linked to the Binance hack moved approximately $594 million in Ether over two days, distributing funds across new wallets and using cross-chain protocols including THORChain and Chainflip in apparent laundering activity.

items.title: SEC freezes assets in alleged $560 million crypto Ponzi scheme
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission froze assets connected to an alleged cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme valued at about $560 million, according to reports summarized in the crypto news cycle.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Tencent launches Hy4 and Hy4 Flash
items.summary: Tencent’s Hy research team released Hy4 and the efficiency-focused Hy4 Flash, accompanied by a live Reddit AMA with researchers. The launch highlights increasing direct engagement between AI labs and developer communities.

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight mixture-of-experts model designed to run with roughly 20 GB of memory. The model uses repeated passes through internal layers and is positioned for laptop-scale deployment and agentic coding.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Carbon, focused on cybersecurity, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, designed for faster coding and agentic workloads. Carbon access is initially limited to vetted cyber defenders, while Hydrogen emphasizes lower cost and faster execution.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding work and GPT-6.2 Sol for lower-cost everyday tasks, with availability in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API. Reports characterize the launch as a performance and pricing update across coding and professional workflows.

items.title: Alibaba makes Qwen4-Max generally available
items.summary: Alibaba opened access to its Qwen4-Max model through QwenCloud and Vercel’s AI Gateway after a limited preview. The model is aimed at developers and uses a sparse architecture with a smaller number of active parameters during inference.

items.title: WM^MLLM proposes editable video world models
items.summary: Researchers introduced WM^MLLM, a multimodal-LLM-based interactive world model that stores world state as an editable panorama with revision history. The approach targets persistent state and editability problems in generated video environments.

items.title: METR expands its AI task-horizon evaluation
items.summary: The evaluation nonprofit METR updated its task-horizon chart with longer and more open-ended tasks. The update indicates continued growth on checkable coding work while showing weaker performance on tasks requiring judgment.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches worldwide and breaks sales records
items.summary: Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Take-Two and Rockstar reported $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales, while the game reportedly sold 32.5 million units through launch-related sales and preorders.[3][7]

items.title: GTA VI sets major livestreaming record
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly generated more than 132 million hours of viewing across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick on launch day, underscoring the scale of the release.[9]

items.title: Ubisoft establishes AI-focused subsidiary
items.summary: Ubisoft reportedly created a new subsidiary called Motherbrain, focused on using artificial intelligence for gameplay innovation, amid a broader restructuring at the publisher.[4]

items.title: Rayman Legends Retold announced for Switch 2
items.summary: Rayman Legends Retold is scheduled to launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on December 3, 2026.[5]

items.title: Town to City wins top Dutch Game Award
items.summary: Town to City received the Best Game award at the 2026 Dutch Game Awards, which recognized projects and companies across 14 categories.[4]

items.title: Bilibili Gaming wins Worlds 2026
items.summary: Bilibili Gaming reportedly defeated its opponent 3–1 to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, giving China another Summoner’s Cup.[6]
